title: Trend of Corporate Bad Debts due to Rising Interest Rates and Assistance for SMEs to Access Capital for Growth
what_it_is: Trend of Corporate Bad Debts due to Rising Interest Rates and Assistance for SMEs to Access Capital for Growth

sections.label: Corporate and SME NPL ratios
sections.summary: Corporate NPL ratio fell from 3.1% in June 2021 to 2.5% in June 2022, and the SME ratio fell from 2.8% to 2.4%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The proportion of non-performing loans (NPL) for the corporate sector has, in fact, fallen over the past year – from 3.1% in June 2021 to 2.5% in June 2022, based on latest available data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The NPL ratio within the SME segment also fell from 2.8% to 2.4% over the same period.

sections.label: SME loan volume growth
sections.summary: SME loan volumes grew 11.5% year-on-year in August 2022, compared to 7.2% growth in broader corporate loans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: SME loan volumes expanded by 11.5% on a year-on-year basis in August 2022, compared to the broader corporate loan growth of 7.2%.

sections.label: Corporate liquidity and support schemes
sections.summary: MAS stress tests show most SGX-listed firms hold sufficient liquidity and would be resilient, while various schemes help SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: The first is that most Singapore-listed firms continue to hold sufficient liquidity as of the first half of 2022 and these are liquid assets, such as cash and cash equivalents, that are exceeding their short-term liabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: And MAS has conducted stress tests on these balance sheets of SGX-listed firms which show that most corporates will be resilient to further interest rate increases and earnings shocks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: In the unlisted sector itself, most firms also either have healthy debt servicing ability or sufficient cash holdings to cover the short-term financing or operational needs, but MAS and the Government will monitor this very closely and adjust where necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Some of these include Enterprise Singapore's Enterprise Financing Scheme which help businesses access and tap into funding and also co-sharing loan default risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: SMEs can also tap on a variety of schemes, such as the Productivity Solutions Grant, Energy Efficiency Grant and SkillsFuture Subsidy, to help them transform their businesses in light of many different challenges afoot.
